The soup is thick with roasted squash, pepper, and a little smoke. A server has folded warm bread into a linen-lined basket beside your elbow. For a moment, the table’s attention loosens enough for you to taste it properly.

Ashara sets down her spoon. “You know it wasn’t earned. Good. That’s a better beginning than pretending it was.”

Rashid’s courtesy sharpens by a degree. “It’s also not merely an opportunity. The human chair has been empty for sixty years. People will attach hopes to you whether you invited them or not.”

“Everyone here has something attached to them,” Thessaly says, brushing sugar from one thumb. “Some of us have it written down.”

Aldric looks along the table. “Bing Bong has been here less than an hour. Perhaps we can permit him one dinner before assigning him the failures of the Council.”

“That would be generous,” Caelindra says, lifting her spoon. “Though it won’t make the failures disappear.”

Seraphel breaks a piece of bread in two.

“The house has waited long.  
It may survive one meal  
without a verdict.”

Ashara’s mouth twitches. Rashid looks briefly toward Seraphel, then returns to his soup.

Across the table, Ysolde has finally taken a sip of water. Her grey eyes settle on the neat repair at your cuff.

“The lawyers selected the other clothes?” she asks. “What did you do before they found you?”
